
 Usage: openajar lane [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

 Browser lanes: one logged-in account each.

╭─ Options ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ --help          Show this message and exit.                                  │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ Commands ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ create               Create a lane with an empty profile. It stays off (not  │
│                      running) until first use. Log in later through          │
│                      browser_view.                                           │
│ import               Create a lane from an existing logged-in profile (for   │
│                      example, one from the first prototype).                 │
│ delete               Remove a lane that is not running. Its profile and      │
│                      files move to OPENAJAR_HOME/trash, nothing              │
│                      is erased.                                              │
│ set-proxy            Move a lane that is not running to another proxy. The   │
│                      lane's sites see a new IP next time, so do this         │
│                      rarely. A lane that has launched needs --yes.           │
│ list                 Lanes on this node: from the running agentosd (which    │
│                      knows which browsers run), else from the store.         │
│ set-device           Move a lane that is not running onto a device, or off   │
│                      it. A lane that has launched gets the device's          │
│                      fingerprint (the browser details a site sees), which is │
│                      a new computer to its site: expect a re-login           │
│                      or a checkpoint (the site asks the account owner a      │
│                      question). That needs --yes. To share a lane's own      │
│                      fingerprint instead, make the device from it: openajar  │
│                      device create <name> --from-lane <lane>.                │
│ sites                The lane's site list: the only hosts its pages may load │
│                      documents from (every navigation, redirect,             │
│                      frame and popup, checked on the node). Empty means no   │
│                      restriction on this lane. `frame:<host>` allows a       │
│                      host only inside a frame (a captcha), never as a page;  │
│                      `accounts.google.@cc` is that host on any of            │
│                      Google's country domains. `suggest` without a platform  │
│                      lists the suggested lists; with one, it adds            │
│                      that list (with the sign-in and captcha hosts every     │
│                      login can need). `strict on` also blocks refused        │
│                      requests before they leave while an agent acts, at the  │
│                      cost of the HTTP cache for that moment. While           │
│                      agentosd runs, a change reaches a running lane at once. │
│                      `observe on <minutes>` (default 60, at most             │
│                      240) records every non-GET request of the lane by its   │
│                      shape (its host, method, path, and the names of         │
│                      its operation and fields, never a value), so you can    │
│                      check the lane's rules against a throwaway              │
│                      account's real traffic.                                 │
│ gate-log             What the commit gate (the check that holds a publish    │
│                      until a person approves exactly what it publishes)      │
│                      classified without a rule while agents drove this lane: │
│                      each request shape (its host, method, path, and         │
│                      the names of its operation and fields, never a value),  │
│                      with how it was classified and how often.               │
│                      `--allow-read <shape>` adds a shape that publishes      │
│                      nothing to the node's read list; `--as-commit <name>    │
│                      --shape <shape>` makes it a named commit rule (the gate │
│                      files it under that name). Either one applies           │
│                      to exactly that host, path and method, on this lane     │
│                      only unless `--all-lanes`. Stored on this node          │
│                      (OPENAJAR_HOME/gate-shapes.json), each change written   │
│                      to the action log; every lane's gate reads it           │
│                      within seconds. `--observed` adds what observe mode saw │
│                      that no commit or write rule matched (a publish         │
│                      the gate takes for a read): name one with               │
│                      `--as-commit`. The owner only.                          │
│ rules                Rule health: when each commit rule (a publish) and      │
│                      write rule (a change that needs only draft              │
│                      permission) last matched on this node; the request      │
│                      shapes no rule covers that each site sent (gated,       │
│                      let through or observed); and what looks like drift: a  │
│                      verified rule that went quiet while its site            │
│                      sends unknown requests of the same kind, a burst of new │
│                      unknown writes, a lane on a site with no rules          │
│                      (its publishes are not gated). Read from the lanes'     │
│                      request logs (names and shapes only, never a            │
│                      value). Fix a stale rule without a code change:         │
│                      `openajar lane gate-log <lane> --as-commit              │
│                      <kind>.<detail> --shape <id>`.                          │
│ pace                 A lane's posting pace: its waking hours, read on the    │
│                      lane's own clock (its proxy's region from its           │
│                      fixed browser fingerprint, unless you set a timezone),  │
│                      the gap between posts and the posts a day. A            │
│                      person driving the lane by hand is never paced; runs    │
│                      and agents are, including runs you start. A             │
│                      publish outside those hours is refused (lane_paced),    │
│                      whatever is approved; a queued or scheduled run         │
│                      moves to the next allowed time. Without options, shows  │
│                      the pace, whose clock it reads and when the lane        │
│                      may post next. Off for every lane until you set one.    │
│ take                 Take control of a lane: agents stop acting on it until  │
│                      you hand it back.                                       │
│ handback             Hand a lane back to agents (also resumes a stopped      │
│                      agent and clears a pending request). The                │
│                      next thing an agent sees on the lane says what changed  │
│                      while you had it.                                       │
│ stop                 Stop the agent on a lane: its runs there are cancelled  │
│                      and nothing acts until you hand it back.                │
│ deny                 Refuse an agent's request for control back. You keep    │
│                      control.                                                │
│ login                Log a lane in by typing into the terminal: openajar     │
│                      reads each sign-in step, asks you for exactly           │
│                      its fields (passwords and codes hidden), and types them │
│                      into the lane's browser at a person's pace.             │
│                      Agents stop on the lane while it runs. Nothing you type │
│                      is logged or shown to an agent.                         │
│ view                 Print a signed live-view link for a lane and the SSH    │
│                      tunnel that reaches it.                                 │
│ freeze               Freeze one lane.                                        │
│ unfreeze             Unfreeze one lane.                                      │
│ forward              Reach a port of a terminal or service lane at           │
│                      http://localhost here, while this command runs.         │
│ redteam              Try to catch our own lanes as bots. Lanes visit a       │
│                      detector site the way an agent drives them              │
│                      (navigate, snapshot, act), and about 30 detectors judge │
│                      what a vendor's sensor and server would                 │
│                      see: keystroke and mouse dynamics, scrolling, focus,    │
│                      navigation and headers, claimed versus                  │
│                      measured hardware, the stealth probe, and lanes linked  │
│                      to each other. Exits 1 when a detector                  │
│                      catches a visit. docs/design/redteam.md says what each  │
│                      detector means.                                         │
│ refresh-fingerprint  Bump the browser version in a lane's pinned fingerprint │
│                      to the installed Camoufox, keeping                      │
│                      every other pinned value (navigator.userAgent and       │
│                      headers.User-Agent change; nothing else).               │
│                      For a lane on a device the change is the device's, so   │
│                      it needs --yes, after the list of every                 │
│                      lane it affects.                                        │
│ check                Is this lane safe to use right now? A checklist per     │
│                      lane: proxy, exit IP and its location,                  │
│                      WebRTC and DNS leaks, profile and pin, signed in (from  │
│                      the cookies already in the profile), the                │
│                      expected account, and any hold. Never warms a lane,     │
│                      opens a page or contacts an account's site.             │
│                      Exits 1 when any lane fails a check.                    │
│ health               One grade per lane from the checks openajar already     │
│                      runs: Looks normal, Check this or Stop, with            │
│                      countable facts and each finding's fix. It reports      │
│                      consistency, leaks and the challenges sites             │
│                      actually showed. It cannot see a site's own risk model, │
│                      the exit IP's reputation or whether a                   │
│                      site's terms allow automation                           │
│                      (docs/RESPONSIBLE-USE.md). Exits 1 when any lane grades │
│                      Stop.                                                   │
│ audit                Does every lane pin one consistent, ordinary device,    │
│                      and do any two lanes pin the same one?                  │
│                      Reads the pinned fingerprints on disk only: no browser  │
│                      starts and nothing is sent (safe on a                   │
│                      node with live lanes). Exits 1 when a pin fails.        │
│                      docs/design/stealth.md lists the rules.                 │
│ stealth-check        Open scratch lanes (no account) in a throwaway home on  │
│                      a test slot and check, the way a page's                 │
│                      own script sees them: automation traces, one consistent │
│                      device, the same device on every launch,                │
│                      no two lanes alike, no WebRTC leak; plus memory per     │
│                      warm lane, wake times and, with --soak-minutes,         │
│                      lanes cycling while browsers are killed. Never touches  │
│                      this node's own lanes, home or ports.                   │
│                      Exits 1 when a check fails. docs/design/stealth.md says │
│                      what each finding means.                                │
│ keepalive            Session keepalive: a short read-only visit to an idle   │
│                      lane's site every few days, inside its waking           │
│                      hours, so its login does not go stale. Shows the next   │
│                      planned visit and the last ones. Off on a node          │
│                      until the owner turns it on (--node on), because it     │
│                      opens real accounts unattended.                         │
│ device               Devices: one fixed browser fingerprint and one proxy    │
│                      shared by a company's lanes.                            │
│ proxy                Proxies that lanes and environments' browsers exit      │
│                      through.                                                │
│ solver               Your own captcha-solving service for every browser (off │
│                      until you add one).                                     │
│ env                  Terminal and service lanes: isolation, programs,        │
│                      shells.                                                 │
│ identity             Signed agent identity (Web Bot Auth) for browser lanes. │
│ vm                   Disposable VMs that agents use as lanes (Hetzner,       │
│                      Morph, Docker or your own machine).                     │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
